There are n patients attending a routine health screening at a clinic. After reviewing the preliminary test results, the nurse gives each patient a sheet listing some patients' names and test result - clear or needs follow-up - that creates an observation matrix. The patients can’t share the given information with others. Each entry (i,k) in the observation matrix indicates whether patient i knows the status of patient k. A value of 1 means patient i knows patient k’s status, while a value of 0 means they do not know. The nurse then publicly announces that at least q patients received a clear result. Then, in repeated rounds, the nurse asks each patient whether they know if their own result is clear. In each round, the patients may rely only on the round number, the answers from the previous rounds, and the observed test results of the other patients.
You are one of the patients, and in round j, you need to answer the question “Did you receive a clear result?” based on what you see, the round number, and the answers from the previous rounds. Answer with “Yes”, “No”, or “I don't know”. Write your answer without additional text and, on a new line, explain your reasoning.
[Example] For example, if there are 2 patients, and the nurse announces that at least 2 patients received a clear result, then in round 1, given the following observation matrix:
[0,1]
[1,0]
you should respond “Yes” for both patients.

There are n patients attending a routine health screening at a clinic. After reviewing the preliminary test results, the nurse gives each patient a sheet listing some patients' names and test result - clear or needs follow-up - that creates an observation matrix. Then, in repeated rounds, the nurse asks each patient whether they know if their own result is clear. In each round, the patients may rely only on the round number, the answers from the previous rounds, and the observed test results of the other patients.

There are n patients attending a routine health screening at a clinic.
